name: Experimental Economics Qualifies Fixed Cohort Institutional Comparison
text: Bougherara, Muller, and Teyssier qualify Kaal's controlled comparison. They explain that experimental economics isolates a causal effect by changing one environmental or institutional feature at a time. Within-subject designs can hold the participants constant across treatments, but they also create an order-effect risk. This supports the methodological rationale for keeping the labor force and work assignment fixed while varying the institution. The correspondence remains narrow. The chapter states a general experimental principle. It does not verify that Kaal's cohort, tasks, or timing were actually held constant. It also does not establish randomization, counterbalancing, independence across conditions, or the validity of any later estimate.
